hook.text: "Some birds can't fly." One example is enough: penguins. In symbols: ∃x (B(x) ∧ ¬F(x)).

buildup.text: The existential quantifier (∃) asserts that at least one member of the domain satisfies the property.

discovery.text: ∃x P(x) is true if there's even one x making P(x) true. Just one is enough.

twist.text: "There exists" is humble. It doesn't say how many—just that the count isn't zero.

climax.text: Existential claims are proven by example. Finding one witness makes the whole statement true.

quiz.question: How do you prove an existential statement?
